title: Retry the doctor version probe past a transient ETXTBSY and name why it failed
action: cargo test runs the bin target's tests as threads in ONE process, so a thread that forks while another has just written an executable leaves the child holding a write fd and the exec returns ETXTBSY. installed_binary_bee_version then returned Failed, binary_freshness_row set probe_failed, the mtime leg had nothing to report because the fixtures are deliberately older, and the row fell through to ok:None. Two freshness tests went red that way - binary_freshness_reports_not_ok_on_a_version_mismatch and binary_freshness_catches_release_drift_when_package_versions_agree - one of them inside the 2.25.2 release gate. Make ExecutableFileBusy the ONE retried spawn error (10 attempts, 20ms apart); every other spawn failure is already a real answer. Give ProbedBeeVersion::Failed a reason string and put it in the unknown row's detail, keeping the literal rs-info in the message because a test asserts it.

truths: ExecutableFileBusy is retried and no other spawn error is
The unknown row's detail names the concrete failure reason
The detail still contains the literal rs-info
The doctor tests survive a 30-run stress loop
The full declared suite is green

trace.outcome: ExecutableFileBusy is retried 10x20ms; the unknown row now names the real failure reason
deviations: First wording of the new detail dropped the literal rs-info and broke binary_freshness_is_unknown_when_the_probe_fails_and_nothing_is_newer on the first stress run; reworded to keep it — the plan was wrong about a fact
trace.inline_reason: Flake triage: diagnosis and fix were one continuous investigation in the main checkout, and only this session is live; splitting the one-function change out to a dispatched worker would have separated the fix from the reproduction loop that proved it
